papers.title_en: CoFlu-Brain: An fMRI Connectivity Foundation Model with Cofluctuation-Based Pretraining
papers.authors: Ziteng Sui, Junfeng Xia, Wenhao Ye, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu
papers.evidence: 基于逐帧共波动预训练的fMRI功能连接基础模型
papers.tldr: 传统fMRI功能连接常把整段扫描压缩为单一Pearson相关矩阵，忽略帧级区域交互波动，且该矩阵受有限BOLD帧影响。CoFlu-Brain将逐帧共波动观测分成保留与丢弃视图，各自汇总为FC矩阵，学习跨保留视图可复现的连接结构，并预测丢弃视图表示，用SIGReg防止表征坍缩。模型在13,444名被试、八个数据集组上预训练，冻结编码器线性探测覆盖七数据集、七项分类和两项年龄预测。多数任务优于已发布模型，随机帧划分提升迁移，完整目标整体最强。
papers.abstract_en: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) commonly characterizes large-scale brain organization through functional connectivity (FC). However, an observed FC matrix is not a fixed brain graph but a statistical estimate determined by the finite BOLD frames used to compute it. Conventional FC-based approaches typically represent each scan with a single Pearson-correlation matrix, leaving frame-resolved variations in regional interactions unexploited. To address this limitation, we introduce CoFlu-Brain, which organizes framewise cofluctuation observations into multiple retained and dropped views, each summarized as an FC matrix. The model learns connectivity structure reproducible across retained views and predicts the representations of the corresponding dropped views, while adopting SIGReg from LeJEPA to prevent representation collapse. We pretrained CoFlu-Brain on 13,444 subjects from eight dataset groups and evaluated its representations via frozen-encoder linear probing on seven classification and two age-prediction tasks across seven datasets. CoFlu-Brain showed strong transfer across demographic, developmental, and clinical prediction tasks, outperforming the evaluated released models on most tasks. Random frame partitioning improved aggregate transfer, while the complete objective achieved the strongest overall performance. Code is available.

papers.title_en: MAGNET: Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network for Connectome Generation
papers.authors: Protyay Dey, Ayush Roy, Hyuna Cho, Won Hwa Kim, Vishnu Suresh Lokhande
papers.evidence: 用于生成功能性脑连接组的流形感知图扩散网络
papers.tldr: 功能脑连接组生成不仅要保证相关矩阵几何有效，还需在粗标签下恢复类别条件几何。MAGNET 采用归一化 Cholesky 表示相关矩阵流形，将噪声隐状态提升为 ROI 区域 token，并以图关系归纳偏置去噪，结合类别锚定条件、摊销结构桥和相关性保持扰动。在 ABIDE、ADNI、OASIS-3 上，类别条件保真度 α,β-F1 提升 7–21%，采样效率更优；仅用二分类标签训练时，零样本子类协方差对齐 λ-MSE 改善超 30%。
papers.abstract_en: Functional brain connectome represents neural connectivity as a matrix of pairwise interactions between brain regions. Generation of functional connectomes is not only a question of validity; rather, having satisfied the constraints on the correlation matrix, the next step is to recover the class-conditional geometry buried under coarse labels. We propose MAGNET, a Manifold-Aware Graph Diffusion Network which uses a normalized-Cholesky representation of the manifold of correlation matrices that guarantees validity. MAGNET lifts noisy latent states into ROI-level region tokens and performs denoising with a relational inductive bias over brain atlas regions. To deal with structural problems induced by coarse labels, MAGNET employs class-anchored conditioning, amortized structural bridge, and relevance-preserving corruption. Across ABIDE, ADNI, and OASIS-3, MAGNET consistently achieves favorable results compared to previous manifold-aware approaches, demonstrating improvements of 7-21% in class-conditional fidelity ($α,β$-F1) across three cohorts and better sampling efficiency. Moreover, while training only with strict binary labels, MAGNET is capable of maintaining clinical heterogeneity through fine substructure of the connectomes in a zero-shot setting, improving subclass covariance alignment ($λ$-MSE) by over 30%. These results suggest that geometric validity is a necessary but insufficient condition for clinical utility in connectome synthesis. Moreover, efforts in making the diffusion denoising class-conditional manifold aware finds utility beyond the highly curved brain connectome generation as this is a critical problem in various general settings. The code repository can be found at https://github.com/protyayofficial/MAGNET.

papers.title_en: HybridDualPathNet: Cross-Fusion Attention of EfficientNetV2 and Swin Transformer for Brain MRI Classification of Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease
papers.evidence: 用于阿尔茨海默与帕金森诊断的脑MRI深度学习分类
papers.tldr: 阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病与健康对照的结构MRI信号存在重叠，且模型性能易受数据划分方式影响，因此跨队列评估与不确定性估计十分关键。本文提出HybridDualPathNet，以EfficientNetV2-S提取局部特征、Swin-Tiny捕获全局上下文，并通过Cross-Fusion Attention进行跨路径融合。在Kaggle图像级划分上准确率达98.25%；在合并Kaggle与ADNI、按来源划分且ADNI患者级隔离的17,859张切片上，准确率73.37%、宏AUC 0.880，来源分层显示Kaggle 91.2%、ADNI 59.2%。温度缩放将ECE从0.130降至0.015，分裂保形预测覆盖89.5%，表明单数据集高分未必能可靠泛化。
papers.abstract_en: Separating Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), and Healthy Controls (HC) using structural MRI remains challenging because disease signatures overlap and model performance can be strongly affected by data partitioning. We present HybridDualPathNet, a hybrid architecture combining EfficientNetV2-S for local features and Swin-Tiny for global context through a Cross-Fusion Attention (CFA) module. We evaluate the model in two experiments. First, on the Kaggle APD-3-Class dataset using an image-level split, the model achieves 98.25% accuracy. Second, on a combined Kaggle and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset containing 17,859 slices, we use a per-source split with patient-wise separation for ADNI subjects. In this setting, the model achieves 73.37% standard accuracy and a macro AUC of 0.880. Source-stratified evaluation reveals a substantial domain gap, with 91.2% accuracy on Kaggle test images and 59.2% on ADNI test images. Temperature scaling reduces expected calibration error from 0.130 to 0.015, while split-conformal prediction achieves 89.5% coverage. Saliency analyses using Grad-CAM++, Integrated Gradients, and occlusion indicate that model activations concentrate on brain tissue. These results highlight the importance of patient-level separation, cross-dataset evaluation, and uncertainty estimation when assessing MRI classification systems. The findings also show that strong performance on a single dataset does not necessarily translate to reliable generalization across imaging cohorts.

papers.title_en: dMRI-F: A Foundation Model for Generalizable Diffusion MRI Analysis from Sparse Acquisitions
papers.authors: Xi Zhu, Yijie Li, Xiaofan Wang, Wei Zhang, Huafu Chen, Ce Zhu, Fan Zhang
papers.evidence: 扩散MRI基础模型与白质连接
papers.tldr: 扩散MRI可揭示脑组织微结构与白质连接，但高质量成像依赖密集采集，扫描时间长且硬件受限。dMRI-F是一种基础模型，以q空间掩码重建预训练，仅用6个体积预测密集多壳数据，学习可泛化的dMRI隐表示。在9个独立数据集上，它统一支持脑区分割、配准与跨模态合成，并优于现有方法，跨采集、人群与任务稳健泛化。该工作为低成本稀疏采集下的通用dMRI分析提供了可扩展框架。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) probes water diffusion within the brain, providing unique information about tissue microstructure and white matter connectivity. High-quality dMRI enables advanced and accurate analyses but demands dense acquisitions, resulting in long scan times and hardware constraints that are often infeasible. Further, dMRI requires dedicated computational methods to support diverse analysis tasks (e.g., parcellation, registration, and synthesis) for both neuroscientific and clinical applications. Here, we present dMRI-F, a foundation model that unifies dMRI data enhancement and downstream tasks across diverse acquisitions and populations, while requiring only minimal acquisition input. dMRI-F is pre-trained with a q-space masked reconstruction task: predicting densely sampled multi-shell data from only six volumes. It learns generalizable latent feature representations of dMRI data, which serve as a core foundation for adapting to diverse downstream tasks, including brain parcellation, brain registration, and cross-modal synthesis. Across nine independently acquired datasets, we demonstrate that dMRI-F outperforms state-of-the-art methods with robust generalization across acquisitions, populations, and tasks. Our results demonstrate dMRI-F's versatility as a general-purpose framework that enables diverse dMRI applications from low-cost, sparse acquisitions.

papers.title_en: CANDLE: Cortical Null-Space Decomposition for Noninvasive Brain Source Imaging
papers.authors: Shuntaro Suzuki, Yuiga Wada, Komei Sugiura
papers.evidence: 基于学习的无创脑源成像
papers.tldr: 无创电生理源成像因源维度远高于传感器观测而严重病态，解不唯一，现有学习法又难泛化到个体皮层几何。CANDLE基于T1 MRI的源-传感器映射，在受试者皮层几何上学习零空间先验，仅建模不可观测源成分并保留几何约束。用1100+皮层几何与26000+脑图模拟训练后，它在仿真源估计及颅内刺激定位、致痫区估计上优于先前方法。这为跨个体几何的非侵入源成像提供了可泛化学习框架。
papers.abstract_en: Electrophysiological source imaging (ESI) aims to estimate cortical source activity from noninvasive electrophysiological measurements such as electroencephalogram (EEG). However, ESI is fundamentally ill-posed because source activity is substantially higher-dimensional than sensor observations, resulting in non-unique solutions. Recent learning-based approaches address this ambiguity by learning data-driven source priors, yet they often struggle to generalize across subject-specific cortical geometries. To address this, we propose CANDLE, a learning-based ESI model that estimates source activity on subject-specific cortical geometries. CANDLE learns a prior over the null space induced by the source-to-sensor mapping derived from T1-weighted MRI, restricting learning to unobservable source components while preserving geometric constraints. To train CANDLE, we develop a whole-brain simulator spanning over 1,100 subject-specific cortical geometries with source configurations derived from over 26,000 statistical brain maps. Trained exclusively on simulated data, CANDLE outperformed prior ESI methods on simulated source activity estimation and generalized to two empirical tasks: (i) intracranial stimulation localization from simultaneously recorded scalp EEG and (ii) epileptogenic zone estimation from presurgical interictal EEG. Our project page is available at https://candle-esi.pages.dev}{https://candle-esi.pages.dev.

papers.title_en: Energy, Information, and the Limits of Neuropsychiatric Classification
papers.authors: Farbod Khodadadi, Mina Kheirkhah, Bita Shariatpanahi, Sarah Alizadeh, Madleen Stenger, Amaia Zurinaga Gutierrez, Shakiba Bakhshian, José C. García Alanis, Nils R. Winter, FOR2107 Consortium, Frank Bremmer, Stefan G. Hofmann, Udo Dannlowski, Tilo Kircher, Sharmili Edwin Thanarajah, Igor Nenadić, Tim Hahn, Hamidreza Jamalabadi
papers.evidence: 神经精神疾病的神经影像标志物与分类极限
papers.tldr: 神经精神疾病神经影像生物标志物长期难以可靠区分，原因未明。作者从统计热力学与神经编码代谢成本出发，提出疾病仅对共享脑活动模式库造成受限形变，从而限制可分类信息。基于FOR2107与SRPBS静息态fMRI，能量景观估计与非线性分类器高度一致（r=0.996）；合成数据与三势阱模型显示，适度形变改变状态占据但最优快照分类仍弱。该框架把物理形变与分类性能联系起来，但人类代谢约束仍待联合测量验证。
papers.abstract_en: Importance: The search for reliable neuroimaging biomarkers of mental disorders has remained elusive despite decades of research. Why clinically consequential disorders yield weak neuroimaging separability remains unresolved. Drawing on statistical thermodynamics and the metabolic costs of neural coding, we propose that psychiatric disorders produce constrained deformations of a largely shared repertoire of brain activity patterns, limiting the class-specific information available for classification.   Observations: We develop a framework linking physical resource constraints, landscape deformation, distributional separation, and attainable classification, and examine its components using human neuroimaging, synthetic data, and an exactly specified physical model. In resting-state fMRI from 1952 FOR2107 participants (823 with major depressive disorder; 1129 healthy controls), held-out energy-landscape estimates and nonlinear classifiers agreed across 13 comparisons (r = 0.996). Similar results emerged at both FOR2107 centers and in 900 SRPBS participants spanning multiple psychiatric diagnoses. In synthetic data, classification improved with distributional separation and approached the optimum. In an equilibrium three-well model, statistical energy equaled physical potential energy scaled by inverse temperature. Modest deformation redistributed state occupancy while optimal snapshot classification remained weak. A literature map found insufficiently comparable evidence to test the human metabolic constraint.   Conclusions: Clinically consequential differences may arise within a largely shared neural repertoire. The thermodynamic framework connects physical deformation to classification under specified assumptions; its metabolic implementation in humans remains untested. Testing this mechanism requires joint measurements of brain activity, bodily physiology, and metabolism.

papers.title_en: BrainAid: Efficient Brain Tumor Detection Using Lightweight CNNs and Explainable AI for Resource-Constrained Environments
papers.authors: Sai Sriram Gonthina, Ross Gore, Bikash Chandra Singh, Pronaya Bhattacharya, Sachin Shetty, Abhishek Phadke, Sandip Roy
papers.evidence: 面向脑MRI肿瘤检测的轻量CNN与可解释AI
papers.tldr: 脑肿瘤MRI人工判读不一致且耗时，深度学习模型又常需大量算力。BrainAid结合轻量CNN与ViT，对胶质瘤、脑膜瘤、垂体瘤和无肿瘤四类MRI进行分类，并引入可解释AI。公开数据集上准确率、精确率、F1均达98%，且部署于Raspberry Pi。它验证了低资源边缘端实时脑肿瘤分类的可行性，可为资源匮乏地区提供快速诊断支持。
papers.abstract_en: A brain tumor is an unusual growth of cells in the brain that can be cancerous or not, affecting normal brain function and causing serious risk to health. Existing solutions for brain tumor classification, such as expert manual evaluations of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, are generally inconsistent as different professionals have different criteria and can be resource-intensive, leading to delayed diagnoses. Additionally, while deep learning models have demonstrated potential, they typically require significant computational resources, motivating the need for more efficient and accessible diagnostic tools that can be deployed in real-time healthcare settings. To address these limitations, this study presents BrainAid, which makes efficient use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for effective classification of four-class classification of glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor MRI scans, outperforming all the standard models such as VGG16, Inception-V3, ResNet-50 and so, while integrating Explainable AI (XAI) to improve interpretability. The BrainAid is trained to classify tumors with a high precision of 98%, achieving an F1 score of 98% and an accuracy of 98% using publicly available dataset. The model is deployed on a Raspberry Pi, demonstrating efficiency in low-resource environments. This system shows the feasibility of real-time, edge-based tumor classification, providing quick diagnostic support for medical professionals and enhancing patient care in resource-limited healthcare facilities and underserved areas.

papers.title_en: BaT-SAM: Introducing Inductive Bias into SAM via a Mixture of Convolutional Experts for Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.authors: Sumiaya Jannat, Md Mahedi Hasan, Md Shamimul Islam, Md Nur Hossain
papers.evidence: 基于SAM自适应的MRI脑肿瘤自动分割
papers.tldr: 脑肿瘤MRI分割对诊疗至关重要，但人工勾画耗时，现有方法泛化有限或依赖用户提示。BaT-SAM通过Conv-LoRA向冻结SAM的ViT编码器注入局部归纳偏置，并用稀疏门控多尺度卷积专家混合增强特征；同时以轻量自提示框回归器实现全自动定位。在BRISC2025上加权平均IoU达0.832并超越SOTA，跨数据集Dice为0.702与0.784。该框架仅微调不足5M参数，为SAM高效适配医学分割提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning; however, manual delineation is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Existing approaches are either task-specific with limited generalization or rely on user-provided prompts during inference. We present BaT-SAM, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework that enables fully automatic brain tumor segmentation with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). BaT-SAM injects local inductive bias into SAM's frozen Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder via Conv-LoRA, where image features are processed by a sparsely gated mixture of multi-scale convolutional experts. This design compensates for the limited translation-equivariant inductive bias of vanilla ViTs while fine-tuning fewer than 5M parameters (less than 1% of the full model). To remove the need for user prompts, we further introduce a lightweight self-prompting box regressor that is jointly optimized with the adapter using scheduled sampling and predicts tumor locations directly from image embeddings. On the BRISC2025 benchmark, BaT-SAM achieves a weighted mean IoU of 0.832 while outperforming state-of-the-art benchmarks. It further demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization, achieving Dice scores of 0.702 on Figshare and 0.784 on the LGG MRI Segmentation dataset.

papers.title_en: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching
papers.authors: Bui Van Hung, Hoang-Son Vo, Mai Duc Minh Huy, Dang Thanh Vu, Soo-Hyung Kim
papers.evidence: 面向神经影像AI的生成式fMRI编码
papers.tldr: 现有fMRI编码多将预测视为确定性回归，难以刻画同一刺激引发的神经响应分布。MultiFlow提出Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching，用可学习时序卷积塑造源均值并以方差头收缩尺度，结合DiT-X速度场、十种冻结视觉/音频/语言/视听骨干融合和按被试Yeo网络头。在Algonauts 2025上，单检查点PCC 0.3163，仅落后1000模型TRIBE集成0.003，并接近VIBE-20与MedARC-50，还能给出刺激条件不确定性。
papers.abstract_en: Current fMRI encoding models frame prediction as deterministic regression, yet identical stimuli evoke a distribution of neural responses (arising from physiological noise, hemodynamic variability, and cognitive fluctuations) that a single point estimate cannot capture. This work introduces MultiFlow, a generative fMRI encoding framework based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and a formulation termed Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching (SISFM). SISFM generalises CFM by conditioning the source distribution on the stimulus: a learnable temporal convolution shapes the source mean with an HRF-length receptive field, while a variance head shrinks its scale, shortening the expected transport path. SISFM is instantiated with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT-X) decoder parameterising the velocity field, with sub-layer Attention Residuals, heterogeneous fusion of ten frozen vision, audio, language, and audiovisual backbones, and per-subject Yeo-network heads. On the Algonauts 2025 dataset, a single MultiFlow checkpoint recovers most of the benefit of large deterministic ensembles: it trails the 1000-model TRIBE ensemble in-distribution by 0.003 PCC (0.3163 vs. 0.3195), and the strongest in- and out-of-distribution ensembles (VIBE-20, MedARC-50) by 0.010 and 0.009 PCC, using a single trained model rather than an ensemble of 20-1000. The same checkpoint also provides stimulus-conditioned uncertainty estimates and sample-based diversity.

papers.title_en: GeoNIRS: Geometry-Aware Pretraining for Heterogeneous fNIRS Representation Learning
papers.authors: Zongsheng Li, Shengyuan Zhu, Zimo Zhang, Hanyao Li, Shengming Wang, Quanying Liu
papers.evidence: 面向异质功能脑成像fNIRS的几何感知预训练
papers.tldr: fNIRS跨数据集联合预训练受通道数、探头布局与任务差异阻碍。GeoNIRS以源-探测器位置为共享空间参考，将变长通道集压缩为固定隐表示，并用HbO/HbR双向交叉重建与连续时间掩码预训练。在8个留出任务上，它取得最高任务平均平衡准确率，线性探测和全微调分别较随机初始化提升4.12与3.30个百分点，且对缺失通道稳健。该工作首次在异构通道配置中显式建模物理通道几何，并开源代码与预训练权重。
papers.abstract_en: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) provides portable and spatially localized measurements of cortical hemodynamics, but differences in channel count, probe layout, signal distribution, and task type hinder joint pretraining across datasets. We introduce GeoNIRS, a geometry-aware framework that uses source-detector locations as a shared spatial reference across heterogeneous probe layouts. GeoNIRS compresses variable-size channel sets into a fixed-size latent representation and employs bidirectional HbO/HbR cross-reconstruction with contiguous temporal masking. GeoNIRS-base is pretrained on eight heterogeneous datasets, while GeoNIRS-large scales to 22 datasets. Neither downstream data nor labels are used during pretraining, enabling evaluation under a strict cross-task setting. To our knowledge, GeoNIRS is the first fNIRS framework to explicitly model physical channel geometry during joint pretraining across heterogeneous channel configurations, and the first to provide complete source code and downloadable pretrained checkpoints. We evaluate GeoNIRS on eight held-out tasks spanning clinical and auditory assessment, pain and affective processing, semantic decoding, and motor function. GeoNIRS achieves the highest task-averaged balanced accuracy among the evaluated conventional machine-learning, fNIRS-specific, general time-series, and fNIRS pretraining baselines. Compared with random initialization, pretraining improves average balanced accuracy by 4.12 percentage points under linear probing and 3.30 points under full fine-tuning, with larger benefits when labels are scarce. GeoNIRS also remains robust to missing input channels. Geometry perturbations and pretraining ablations further show that both channel geometry and cross-chromophore reconstruction contribute to the learned representations.
